description: The high-performance, All-metal tungsten! Weldclass RE4 purple-tip TIG Tungsten electrodes are suitable for both DC (Steel, Stainless steel etc) and AC (Aluminium) TIG welding. Maintains tip shape, reliable arc striking, low burn off rate, long service life and smooth/stable arc.
short: The high-performance, All-metal tungsten! Weldclass RE4 purple-tip TIG Tungsten electrodes are suitable for both DC (Steel, Stainless steel etc) and AC (Aluminium) TIG welding. Maintains tip shape, reliable arc striking, low burn off rate, long service life and smooth/stable arc.

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES

  • Universal: "All metal" Tungsten Suitable for DC (Steel, Stainless steel etc) and AC (Aluminium)
  • Convenient: Replaces virtually all other types of Tungstens, including; Thoriated (red tip) & Zironiated (white tip)
  • Safe: Unlike Thoriated (red tip) tungstens, does Not contain radioactive elements = No special safeguards required for use, storage or transport
  • High Performance: Maintains tip geometry, reliable arc striking, low burn off rate, long service life and smooth/stable arc


APPLICATION INFO:

  • DC welding of mild steel, stainless steel, copper and chrome molly
  • AC TIG welding of: Aluminum alloys and Aluminum bronze


WHAT ELSE?

  • A Hazard-Free (non-radioactive) Replacement for Thoriated electrodes
  • Also replaces Zirconiated, Lanthanated and other electrodes
  • Purple (Turquoise) Colored Tip
  • Contains additives/combinations of "rare-earth" oxides, scientifically balanced to provide optimum arc characteristics and wear life
  • Compared to other tungsten formulas: Requires less energy to start, Runs cooler, Longer Electrode Life, Greater current capacity (ability to use a smaller-diameter electrode for the same job or use higher current for a similar-sized electrode)

Material Thickness vs Amps vs Tungsten Size

Because of the many variables in any given TIG welding application, there is no single formula to say "for X thickness you need X amps".

The many factors that influence this include; material being welded, type of tungsten elecrode used, type of weld joint, weld position, operator technique, skill and/or experience, required strength or quality of the weld joint, etc.

However, here is a rough guide for TIG welding of steel, stainless or aluminium:

Material
Thickness* Suggested
Tungsten
Size* Amps
Required* <1mm 1.0mm 10-30A <2mm 1.6mm 30-80A 2-3mm 2.4mm 80-150A 4-5mm 3.2mm 150-200A

*This is a general guide only and should not be used as specific advice for any particular application

KEY FEATURES

  • 7-Year Warranty offer*
  • Internal pressure relief safety valve*
  • One-piece encapsulated seat
  • Heavy-duty Platinum series, no quality shortcuts
  • Proven reliability
  • Complies with AS4267

SPECIFICATIONS & APPLICATION INFO:

  • Suitable for oxygen gases
  • Output: 0-1,000 kpa
  • Inlet / cylinder connection: AS2473 Type 10
  • Outlet connection: 5/8" UNF Male RH

INTERNAL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE

  • Risk of over-pressurisation of the regulator body is a safety hazard when using high pressure gas (such as oxygen or argon/CO2) and can cause rupture / explosion of the regulator and or components
  • The pressure relief valve prevents over-pressurisation
  • Valve is built into regulator body internal parts, protecting it from contamination, damage or tampering, to ensure reliable operation

WHY USE WELDCLASS OXY/ACETYLENE HEATING TIPS ?

  • Proven Quality
  • Precision Machined = Prevents flashback & back-fire

APPLICATION INFO:

  • For use with oxygen/acetylene
  • Connects to P4-SHB Tube/Barrel

OPERATOR INFO:

Heating with Oxy/Acetylene has limitations and hazards. Care must be taken to ensure that the maximum draw-off consumption rate of acetylene is not exceeded (consult your gas supplier for details). For this reason, Acetylene tips are available only up to size 2.

Where possible, Weldclass recommends that Oxy/LPG be used in preference to Oxy/Acetylene. LPG is safer and less prone to flashback or backfire, and larger tip sizes are available for heavy heating. LPG is also often only a fraction of the cost of Acetylene.

FAQs:

Q: The 10-25 connector from Weldclass (or other supplier) does not fit/tighten correctly to the connector on my welding machine, why?
A: Due to their compact size, "10-25" male and female Dinse connectors must be manufactured with tight tolerances to ensure a secure fit. However, many manufacturers don't or can't meet these precise standards, leading to a common industry problem: a 10-25 male connector from one brand may not properly fit the female connector from a different connector/machine brand.
This problem is particularly common with welding machines supplied by less experienced brands that use low-quality component suppliers.
Weldclass 10-25 connectors are specifically engineered to accommodate these variations and fit as many brands as possible. However, due to inconsistent sizing across the industry, there may still be instances where Weldclass connectors do not fit some machines. In such cases, we recommend trying an alternative connector brand or sourcing a connector directly from the machine’s manufacturer.

description: Promax K4 series air arc gouging torch / handpiece and spares. Robust & durable design. Now available with 7-year warranty
short: Promax K4 series air arc gouging torch / handpiece and spares. Robust & durable design. Now available with 7-year warranty

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • 7-Year Warranty Offer*

SPECIFICATIONS:

  • Max Capacity: 800A
  • Cable size: 50mm 2
  • Cable length: 2.1m (7 ft)
  • Compressed Air Inlet Connection: 5/8" UNF female thread with nut & 10mm hose tail fitted
  • Power Connection: Lug / eyelet


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Highly efficient metal removal, defect & crack repairs, weld removal, edge preparation, etc
  • Use with gouging carbon rods + DC power source + compressed air
  • Use with 5mm - 13mm gouging carbons
  • Requires DC Power Source with minimum 300 Amps output


HOW IT WORKS;

  • Air arc gouging process is similar to arc/stick welding, in some respects. The gouging torch/handpiece holds a gouging carbon rod, like a stick welding electrode holder.
  • The carbon rod creates an arc when in contact with the metal workpiece and is consumed during gouging.
  • The torch is connected to a welding machine / power source and to compressed air supply.
  • When the air valve on handpiece is opened, this forces air down through a copper jaw/nozzle, and down one side of the carbon rod.
  • The operator drags the carbon rod across the job, this creates molten metal in the "arc zone" which is then pushed away by the air jet.
  • Gouging carbons are available in different sizes, the choice of size will depend on the capacity of the welder / power source and/or the volume/thickness of metal to be removed.


TYPICAL SET UP:

Following is a commonly-used configuration. Note this can vary depending on the welder/power source and user preferences.

Power Cable/ Connections:

  • Short length of welding cable with cable lug on one end and male cable joiner/connector on the other.
  • This short cable is bolted to terminal on gouging torch cable, other end is connected/joined to a longer cable.
  • Longer cable is connected back to the welding machine / power source.
  • Cable size will depend on: amperage capacity required, welding or power source capacity, and/or gouging carbon rod size used. As minimum amps required for gouging are around 300A, cable size used is typically at least 35mm 2 or 50mm 2 .

Air Hose / Connections:

  • Short length of 10mm ID air hose, one end crimped to air fitting/nipple on gouging torch cable terminal & other end fitted with male air fitting (eg nitto style, or user preference).
  • Short air hose is then connected to longer air supply hose from air compressor.

faq.q: What shade range does the PROMAX 200 have?
faq.a: The PROMAX 200 Welding Helmet has a variable shade range of 9-13 for MIG and Stick welding. It also has sensitivity and delay adjustments, plus a grind-mode switch that locks the lens in its light shade so you can grind without lifting the helmet.

faq.q: Is the PROMAX 200 suitable for TIG welding?
faq.a: Weldclass lists the PROMAX 200 Welding Helmet as ideal for MIG and Stick welding in light to medium fabrication and occasional use. TIG is not listed for this model. The PROMAX 350, 500 and 650 helmets list TIG welding in their applications.

faq.q: How big is the PROMAX 200 viewing area?
faq.a: The PROMAX 200 Welding Helmet has a 96 x 39mm viewing area with a 1/1/1/2 optical rating. It also has a magnification lens holder that takes standard magnification lenses, which helps welders who would otherwise wear reading glasses under the helmet.

faq.q: What is the difference between the PROMAX 180 and PROMAX 200?
faq.a: The PROMAX 200 Welding Helmet adds a grind-mode switch that locks the lens in light shade, and is rated for light to medium fabrication. Both helmets share shade 9-13, sensitivity and delay controls, a 96 x 39mm view and 1/1/1/2 optics. RRP is $110 for the 200 and $89 for the 180.

faq.q: What warranty comes with the PROMAX 200?

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • 7-Year Warranty* *
  • Enjoy a Generous Viewing Area (100 x 53mm), with Ultra-Clear Vision
  • Dual Shade Range 5-8 / 9-13 plus grind mode to cover a wide range of welding processes
  • 4 Arc Sensors for reliable arc detection & switching
  • Lightweight, Comfortable & Easy to use


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Light to Medium Fabrication, Rural, Maintenance, etc
  • MIG welding
  • Stick welding
  • TIG welding down to 30 amps
  • Grinding
  • Plasma Cutting
  • Air-Arc Gouging


FUNCTIONS:

  • Welding mode: Variable shade 5-8 / 9-13
  • Grind mode: Locks lens to light mode (shade 4)
  • Delay: Adjustable 0.1-1.0s (switching time from dark back to light after welding arc stops)
  • Sensitivity: Adjustable low-high


OTHER FEATURES:

  • Viewing area: 100 x 53mm
  • High-Impact tested and rated to Australian standard AS1337.1
  • Auto-darkening lens complies with AS1338.1
  • 'Hinge & Lock' Lens Retainer System = Easy cover lens replacement, Seals tightly against spatter to prevent damage to electronic lens
  • Magnification lens holder - takes standard magnification lenses
  • Reliable Power Source: Replaceable battery plus solar assist, efficient electronics for low power consumption
  • 'Full Laminate' Lens Construction: Each layer in the electronic lens assembly is firmly laminated for superior optical quality and long service life. This is in contrast to cheaper lenses which are simply glued on the edge and, over time, are prone to contamination and failure.
  • Lightweight, Durable and Shock Resistant shell
  • Auto-on & Auto-off = No buttons to press, Hassle-Free operation


COMMON SPARE PARTS & OPTIONAL ACCESSORIES

  • Clear cover lens kit (2 outer, 1 inner) WC-05335
  • Clear cover lens outer Pk10 WC-05323
  • Inner cover lens Pk5 WC-05321
  • Magnification lenses
  • Headgear WC-05325
  • Sweatband WC-01630
  • Batteries: Type CR2032, commonly available from any battery retailer/wholesaler (Weldclass does not supply this item)

faq.q: Can the PROMAX 350 be used for TIG welding?
faq.a: Yes. The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet is rated for TIG welding down to 30 amps, plus MIG, Stick, grinding, plasma cutting and air-arc gouging. For TIG work below 30 amps, the PROMAX 500 and PROMAX 650 are rated down to 5 amps.

faq.q: What is the viewing area of the PROMAX 350?
faq.a: The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet has a 100 x 53mm viewing area, which Weldclass says is larger than many helmets in its class. Four arc sensors handle arc detection and switching, and the dual shade range of 5-8 and 9-13 covers a wide range of processes.

faq.q: What battery does the PROMAX 350 use?
faq.a: The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet runs on a replaceable CR2032 battery with solar assist. Weldclass does not supply the battery, but CR2032 cells are widely available from battery retailers. The helmet turns on and off automatically, with no power button to press.

faq.q: What is the PROMAX 350 warranty and price?
faq.a: The PROMAX 350 Welding Helmet has an RRP of $158 incl. GST in Blue or Aussie Graphic, sold through Weldclass distributors. It carries a 2-year standard warranty on the auto-darkening lens, with a 7-year offer that requires online registration within 30 days of purchase.

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • 7-year Warranty *
  • Super-Size 85cm 2 Viewing Area: 98 x 87mm, with Ultra-Clear 1/1/1/1 rated optics
  • Dual Shade Range 5-8 / 9-13 plus grind mode to cover a wide range of welding processes
  • 4 Arc Sensors for reliable arc detection & switching
  • Light weight, Comfortable & Easy to use (weighs 560g)


APPLICATION INFO:

  • MIG welding
  • Stick welding
  • TIG welding down to 5 amps
  • Grinding
  • Plasma Cutting
  • Air-Arc Gouging


FUNCTIONS:

  • Welding mode: Variable shade 5-8 / 9-13
  • Delay: Adjustable 0.1-1.0s (switching time from dark back to light after welding arc stops)
  • Sensitivity: Adjustable low-high
  • Grind mode: Locks lens to light mode (shade 4)


OTHER FEATURES:

  • High-Impact tested and compliant to Australian standard AS/NZS 1337.1
  • Auto-darkening lens complies with AS/NZS 1338.1
  • 'Hinge & Lock' Lens Retainer System = Easy cover lens replacement, Seals tightly against spatter to prevent damage to electronic lens
  • Magnification lens holder - takes standard magnification lenses
  • Reliable Power Source: Replaceable battery plus solar assist, efficient electronics for low power consumption
  • 'Full Laminate' Lens Construction: Each layer in the electronic lens assembly is firmly laminated for superior optical quality and long service life. This is in contrast to cheaper lenses which are simply glued on the edge and, over time, are prone to contamination and failure.
  • Lightweight, Durable and Shock Resistant shell
  • Auto-on & Auto-off = No buttons to press, Hassle-Free operation


COMMON SPARE PARTS & OPTIONAL ACCESSORIES:

  • Clear cover lens kit (2 outer, 1 inner) WC-05336
  • Clear cover lens outer Pk10 WC-05324
  • Inner cover lens Pk5 WC-05322
  • Magnification lenses
  • Sweatband WC-01630
  • Headgear WC-05325
  • Batteries: Type CR2450, commonly available from any battery retailer/wholesaler (Weldclass does not supply this item)

faq.q: How big is the PROMAX 500 viewing area?
faq.a: The PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet has a 98 x 87mm viewing area, about 85cm², with 1/1/1/1 rated optics. That is the largest window in the PROMAX 180 to 500 range, and reviewers frequently mention it as the main reason they bought the helmet.

faq.q: Can the PROMAX 500 be used for TIG welding?
faq.a: Yes. The PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet is rated for TIG welding down to 5 amps, along with MIG, Stick, grinding, plasma cutting and air-arc gouging. Four arc sensors give reliable switching, and the dual shade range of 5-8 and 9-13 covers low and high amperage work.

faq.q: What battery does the PROMAX 500 use?
faq.a: The PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet uses a replaceable CR2450 battery with solar assist. Weldclass does not supply the battery, but CR2450 cells are commonly available from battery retailers and wholesalers. The helmet switches on and off automatically, so there are no buttons to press.

faq.q: Does the PROMAX 500 meet Australian standards?
faq.a: Yes. The PROMAX 500 Welding Helmet is high-impact tested and compliant to AS/NZS 1337.1, and its auto-darkening lens complies with AS/NZS 1338.1. It weighs 560g and carries a 2-year standard lens warranty, with a 7-year offer that requires online registration within 30 days of purchase.

short: 108x51mm magnification lenses for welding helmets. Suits: Flip-front helmets, Weldclass Promax series helmets & various other brands/models. meta.more:
FEATURES / SPECIFICATIONS

  • For a magnified view of the work area
  • Improves clarity of vision & detail
  • Size 108 x 51mm
  • Suitable for standard flip front helmets & various auto-darkening helmets
  • Suits Weldclass (all models), and many other helmet brands/models


FAQs:

Q: Do magnification lenses come in sizes larger than 108x51mm?
A: Currently 108x51mm is the only size available. Due to high tooling costs, these are not produced in other sizes. On Weldclass & some other helmets, you can adjust the mag lens position so it is in your direct line of sight.

Q: Is the a correct way to fit magnification lenses?
A: Magnification lenses will work either way, but to prevent / minimise fogging, it is best to place the flat side of the magnification lens towards the auto-darkening lens, and curved side towards the welder's face.

KEY FEATURES:

  • Free Zip-Ties and Curtain Rings Supplied with Each Curtain - Ready to Install, no need to purchase additional accessories
  • Long-Life Construction: Double Hem with Heavy Duty Brass Eyelets
  • Available in Red or Green
  • Fire retardant
  • Tested & Conforms to EN ISO 25980


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Designed to protect workers from indirect welding flash
  • Allows natural light into work areas


SPECIFICATIONS:

  • Eyelet spacing - Top & Bottom: Every ~200mm
  • Eyelet spacing - Sides: Every ~600mm
  • Eyelet size: 10-12mm I.D.
  • Curtain ring size: approx 50mm diameter
  • Tested & conforms to ISO 25980
  • Material: Treated PVC ~0.4mm



FAQs:

Apart from the colour, is there any difference between red & green curtains?
No. Weldclass red & green curtains meet the same safety requirements/specifications, the only difference is the colour.

Are curtains available in larger / custom sizes ?
No. Weldclass only supply curtains in the sizes listed. The class of curtains offered by Weldclass are intended to be an affordable & easy-to-install solution, for use in applications such as fitting to portable frames or curtain wire/rods. For applications such as; custom sizes, curtain is needed to span wider/longer areas, permanent / long-term fixture, heavy traffic, heavy industrial use, etc we recommend suppliers such as Flexshield who offer customised/bespoke solutions.

Are curtains available in rolls ?
No. Weldclass only supply pre-made curtains in the sizes listed. Note that each curtain is hemmed and includes eyelets. Bulk curtain material, even if available, would not include hems or eyelets.

KEY FEATURES:

  • Heavy Duty Split Cowhide Leather
  • Sewn with Heat-Resistant Kevlar Thread, for resistance to seam failure
  • With eyelets (see details below)


APPLICATION INFO:

  • For protection against grinding sparks, light to medium spatter, indirect heat
  • NOT recommended for protection against slag or molten droplets or direct flame

SPECIFICATIONS

  • Temperature Resistance: Up to 200 ° c short duration (see more info below)
  • Nominal Thickness: 1.2mm
  • Nominal Weight: 900-1,100g/m2
  • Stitching: Heat-resistance Kevlar
  • Colour: Chrome / grey
  • Material: Cowhide split leather


EYELET SPACING:

  • On each corner & every 900/1,000mm
  • 1x2m: Does not have eyelets
  • 1.8x1.8m & 2x2m = Total 8 eyelets
  • 3x3m = Total 12 eyelets

INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE

  • If protecting critical or costly surfaces / items, allways use more layers initially, and test on a non-critical surface first
  • When using for surface protection: If possible use on an incline of at least 15 degrees, or when neccessary to use in horizontal position add more layers
  • Where the blanket is in closer proximity to the source of sparks etc, consider adding more layers of blanket/fabric as the sparks/spatter will have less time to cool and will be at a higher temperature at the point of touching/impact with the blanket
  • Use hand, eye and respiratory protection during handling and use, to protect against airborn fibres and any dust/debris that has fallen on the blanket during use
  • While leather blankets will withstand up to 200 ° c, a safety margin should always be allowed for, especially in critical applications. C onsider using WB550 , WB1000 , WB1100 , or WB1250+ blankets for more demanding applications
  • Worn or damaged blankets will compromise protection and should be replaced

TEMPERATURE RESISTANCE OF COWHIDE LEATHER

Cowhide split leather fibre will typically withstand up to 200° c short term exposure and 80° c continuous exposure. Note that leather is typically higher in density and homogeneity when compared to woven fabrics (such as fibreglass or silica), increasing durability and resistance to penetration by sparks etc . Whilst the outer leather fibres in direct contact with a hot spark/particle may char or burn, the highly compact leather fibres resist further penetration allowing the partical to cool before it can fully penetrate the blanket. For this reason, leather blankets are a popular choice for light to medium welding applications where sparks and spatter will typically cool rapidly before and after contact with the blanket.

*As applications and usage conditions vary widely, no warranty or fitness for use in any specific application is implied or intended. In critical applications, blankets should always be tested/trialed to determined if they offer adequate protection. Being a natural product, leather properties will vary and this information is indicative only. E.&O.E.

FAQs:

  • Why hook & loop closure, instead of press studs?
    • Press studs are prone to tearing out - this is because the force of opening the stud is concentrated on the small area of leather it is attached to and this gradually becomes fatigued every time the jacket is opened/closed
    • Preventing this requires adding layers of reinforcement leather which adds unnecessary weight to the garment.
    • Studs also conduct heat (& electrical current) and should be insulated. Use of hook & loop keeps the garment as light as possible, and provide a better seal against spatter/sparks.
    • The opening on Promax BL7 jackets is offset, to keep the hook & loop away from the "high wear" area directly in front the operator. The "overlap" is also positioned so that the hook & loop is not exposed to sparks etc coming from the work area directly in front of the wearer. This helps to extend the garment life.
  • Is it possible to wash the PROMAX BL7 Blue Leather Jacket?
    • Leather should not be washed with water & should be dry-cleaned only. We recommend that you consult your dry cleaner for further advice.

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • 7-Year Warranty*
  • Lighter & Cooler than Full Leather, with Leather Sleeves for Heavy Duty Protection where it is most needed
  • Designed & manufactured with attention to detail
  • Includes practical features like Pockets, Pen Holders, and Satin-lined shoulders for easier wear/removal
  • Riveted stress points & Double-stitched with Kevlar = Longer garment life In tough conditions

APPLICATION INFO:

  • For Protection During Welding, Cutting & Grinding
  • Used by Professional Welders, Workshop Supervisors & Assistants, Students

WHAT ELSE ?

  • 100% Cotton Specially Treated for Flame-Resistance: Durable and More Comfortable than Cotton/Polyester Material
  • Leather Sleeves made from Top Quality Cowhide Sourced from America & Italy. Remains Supple & Durable for Longer.
  • Double-Stitched with Kevlar Heat-Resistant Thread with Rivets at Pressure-Points (eg: Cuffs) to Prevent Seam Failure
  • Opening: Wide Hook & Loop Style Strip for Long Lasting, Firm Closure. No Studs to Tear Off.
  • Pen Pocket on Both Arms: Handy Spot for Markers, Scribers, Small Rules, etc
  • Large Pocket on Both Sides with Hook & Loop Style Closure: Keep Tools & Parts within Reach, Flap Prevents Debris Entering Pocket
  • Satin-Lined Shoulders and Arms allow garment to easily slide on and off

SIZE INFO:

Approx' Chest circumference in cm:

  • M=121
  • L=127
  • XL=137
  • 2XL=147
  • 3XL=157

FAQs:
Why hook & loop closure, instead of press studs?

  • Press studs are prone to tearing out - this is because the force of opening the stud is concentrated on the small area of material it is attached to, and this gradually becomes fatigued every time the jacket is opened/closed. This is especially problematic for FR material, where the material is not as thick/dense as leather.
  • Preventing this requires adding layers of reinforcement material which adds unnecessary weight and cost to the garment.
  • Studs also conduct heat (& electrical current) and require insulating.
  • Studs do not provide complete closure, the gaps between each stud can be penetrated by spatter, sparks, etc.
  • Use of hook & loop keeps the garment as light as possible, and provide a better seal against spatter/sparks.

Is it possible to wash the this Jacket?

  • Because of the leather sleeves, this jacket cannot be washed with water & should be dry-cleaned only. We recommend that you consult your dry cleaner for further advice.

*Standard warranty 3 months, with extended 7 year warranty available if registered online after purchase.

WELDCLASS "Promax" Series: No shortcuts, Great value!


KEY FEATURES 'PROMAX HV2' JACKETS ?

  • 7-Year Warranty*
  • Hi-Visibility Material with Reflective Tape for Day/Night use
  • Harness Compatible: Rear Opening/Flap Allows use with Safety Harness, if required
  • 100% Flame Resistant, including the Silver Reflective Tape
  • Extended Back: Protects Lower Back when Bending, Kneeling, etc

APPLICATION INFO:

  • For Protection During Welding, Cutting & Grinding
  • Harness Compatibility permits use on sites where safety/fall harnesses are required
  • For all day/night applications where high visibility is required

WHAT ELSE ?

  • Double-Stitched with Heat-Resistant Kevlar Thread, with Rivets at Pressure-Points (eg: Cuffs) to Prevent Seam Failure
  • Rear Opening Flap for safety harness cable / umbilical cord or air breathing hoses
  • Includes Practical Features Like; Pockets, Pen Holders, and Satin-Lined Shoulders for Easier Wear/Removal
  • 100% Cotton Specially Treated for Flame-Resistance - Lighter & Cooler than Full Leather
  • Leather Sleeves made from Top Quality Cowhide Sourced from America & Italy. Remains Supple & Durable for Longer.
  • Opening: Wide Hook & Loop Style Strip for Long Lasting, Firm Closure. No Studs to Tear Off.

SIZE INFO:

  • Approx' Chest Measurement in cm:
    • M=121
    • L=127
    • XL=137
    • 2XL=147
    • 3XL=157
    • 4XL=167

FAQs:

  • Why hook & loop closure, instead of press studs?
    • Press studs are prone to tearing out - this is because the force of opening the stud is concentrated on the small area of material it is attached to, and this gradually becomes fatigued every time the jacket is opened/closed. This is especially problematic for FR material, where the material is not as thick/dense as leather.
    • Preventing this requires adding layers of reinforcement material which adds unnecessary weight and cost to the garment.
    • Studs also conduct heat (& electrical current) and require insulating.
    • Studs do not provide complete closure, the gaps between each stud can be penetrated by spatter, sparks, etc.
    • Use of hook & loop keeps the garment as light as possible, and provide a better seal against spatter/sparks.
  • Is it possible to wash the this Jacket?
    • Because of the leather sleeves, this jacket cannot be washed with water & should be dry-cleaned only. We recommend that you consult your dry cleaner for further advice.

*Standard warranty 3 months, with extended 7 year warranty available if registered online after purchase.

meta.who: Suits farm, home workshop and onsite fabricators welding mild or galvanised steel outdoors without gas.

faq.q: What is PLATINUM GL-11 gasless wire used for?
faq.a: PLATINUM GL-11 Gasless MIG Wire is an E71T-11 self-shielded wire for welding mild and galvanised steel without shielding gas. It is all-positional and suits single or multi-pass welds, which makes it a common choice for outdoor, onsite and windy jobs such as fencing and cattle yards.

faq.q: Can PLATINUM GL-11 weld rusty or painted steel?
faq.a: Weldclass says PLATINUM GL-11 Gasless MIG Wire is easy to use even on steel that is moderately rusty, dirty or painted. It is also low fume and gives easy de-slagging. Reviewers report good results on galvanised and painted tube as well as general farm and repair work.

faq.q: What sizes does PLATINUM GL-11 come in?
faq.a: PLATINUM GL-11 Gasless MIG Wire is listed in 0.8mm, 0.9mm and 1.2mm on 200mm 4.5kg spools, and in 0.9mm and 1.2mm on 300mm 15kg spools. RRP starts at $92.95 for a 4.5kg spool and $325 for 15kg, incl. GST, through Weldclass distributors.

faq.q: Should I use 0.8mm or 0.9mm PLATINUM GL-11 for thin steel?
faq.a: PLATINUM GL-11 Gasless MIG Wire is available in 0.8mm on a 4.5kg spool for thin section work, alongside 0.9mm. Weldclass publishes a guide on choosing between 0.8mm and 0.9mm gasless wire for thin steel, and one reviewer noted 0.8mm is easier on thin sheet.

name: Electrodes - Hardfacing PROMAX 700
description:
700 series hardfacing welding rods for general hard-facing of ground-engaging implements and similar applications. Good abrasion resistance with moderate-to-high impact strength, typical hardness 53-56 HRC. A tough weld deposit also makes this electrode suitable for parts subject to fatigue or flexing in service. Suitable for a wide range of applications including the surfacing of post hole augers, agricultural points, shares and tynes, grader and cultivator blades, etc. Supplied in 1kg re-usable convenience pack to keep electrodes in good condition. For higher abrasion resistance and longer wear life, we recommend Platinum 943 series electrodes .

KEY FEATURES:

  • User Friendly: Very Smooth & Stable Arc, Easy Striking, Low Spatter, Easy Slag Removal
  • Hydrogen controlled, for welding mild & high-strength (carbon-manganese) steels up to 510MPa
  • All-Positional (except for vertical down) & excellent weld appearance
  • Twin-coated


2KG VACUUM FOIL SEALED PACKS - REDUCES WASTE & MOISTURE EXPOSURE !

  • Vacuum foil sealed packs keeps moisture out, right up to the point of use
  • Smaller pack size reduces waste & minimises exposure to atmospheric moisture


WHY IS IT IMPORTANT TO AVOID MOISTURE ?

  • Air contains moisture (humidity) and any electrode exposed to air will absorb moisture
  • This increases hydrogen levels in the electrode (water 'H2O' contains hydrogen 'H')
  • Increased hydrogen compromises the strength & mechanical properties of the weld
  • Moisture can also negatively affect the arc characteristics of the electrode


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Mining maintenance & fabrication
  • Structural steel & site welding
  • Rural maintenance
  • Pipe construction
  • Boilers & pressure vessels
  • Build up or buffer layer prior to hard facing
  • Single sided weld joints
  • Suitable for all DC or AC welding machines


CLASSIFICATIONS:

  • AWS A5.1 E7016 H8
  • AS/NZS 1553.1 (old) E4946
  • AS/NZS 4855: (new) B E4916 A U H10

FAQs:

Q: Does the vacuum foil seal avoid the need for pre-drying electrodes in an oven?
A: This depends on the application. At the point of opening a sealed pack, 16XT electrodes will almost certainly contain less moisture than electrodes that are not vacuum sealed - however electrodes ovens should still be used in critical situations or when specified in the weld procedure.

Q: How many rods per pack/KG ?
2.6mm = approx. 50 rods per KG / 100 rods per 2kg pkt
3.2mm = approx. 33 rods per KG / 66 rods per 2kg pkt

faq.q: Does the FORCE 160MST come with a gas regulator?
faq.a: No. The FORCE 160MST standard package (WF-06127, RRP $659 incl. GST) includes the machine, a 3m BZL 15 Euro-connect MIG torch, 3m earth and stick leads and drive rollers for 0.8/0.9mm solid and gasless wire. A gas regulator (4-AR1) and gas hose kit (WC-03338) are optional for gas MIG.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 160MST weld aluminium?
faq.a: The FORCE 160MST can MIG weld aluminium using 0.9/1.0mm aluminium wire, and the MK2 model is spool gun ready. It cannot TIG weld aluminium, which needs AC/DC TIG capability such as the FORCE 201T. Its DC lift-arc TIG suits steel, stainless, copper and chromoly up to 3mm.

faq.q: What is the difference between the FORCE 160MST MK1 and MK2?
faq.a: The FORCE 160MST MK2, launched February 2024 (serial numbers starting 2023 or later), has a Euro-connect MIG torch (WC-03609) that screws onto the front and is spool gun ready. The MK1 (serial 2022 or earlier) has a direct-connect torch (WC-06225) wired inside the machine and no spool gun capability.

faq.q: How thick can the FORCE 160MST weld?
faq.a: The FORCE 160MST has a maximum recommended MIG capacity of 6mm mild steel, from 160A output at 20% duty cycle. In stick mode it runs 2.0-3.2mm electrodes up to 140A, and in DC lift-arc TIG mode it welds steel, stainless, copper and chromoly up to 3mm.

faq.q: What warranty does the FORCE 160MST have?
faq.a: The FORCE 160MST comes with a 2-year standard warranty. Weldclass extends this to 7 years when the machine is registered online within 30 days of purchase, so register it as soon as you buy it from your Weldclass distributor.

faq.q: How thick can the FORCE 45P cut?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter clean cuts up to 20mm mild steel, 18mm stainless steel and 14mm aluminium. Its severance capacity is 25mm mild steel, 22mm stainless steel and 20mm aluminium. Severance means it will part the metal, with a rougher edge than a clean cut.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 45P run on a generator?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter has Power Factor Correction, which reduces power draw and makes it suited to generator use. Weldclass specifies a generator of at least 8kVA, ideally 10kVA or more. PFC also lets it run on extension leads up to 100m long.

faq.q: What air compressor do I need for the FORCE 45P?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter needs a compressor that delivers at least 120L/min (4.5cfm) free air delivery. An air regulator with filter and Nitto style fitting is included. Weldclass recommends the optional PLATINUM Z-20 air filter for longer parts life and better cutting performance.

faq.q: What plug does the FORCE 45P have?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter comes fitted with a 15A 240V plug on a 3m input lead, so it needs a 15A outlet. Off the grid, Weldclass specifies a generator of at least 8kVA, ideally 10kVA or more. Power Factor Correction lets it run on extension leads up to 100m.

faq.q: What warranty comes with the FORCE 45P?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter has a 2-year standard warranty. Weldclass offers an extended 7-year warranty, which requires online registration within 30 days of purchase. The FORCE 45P is sold through Weldclass distributors at an RRP of $1,690 incl. GST.

FITTING THESE TORCHES TO OTHER MACHINE BRANDS / MODELS:

  1. Control Plug Connection
    • While basic TIG torches with manual gas-valve or basic on/off switch are usually interchangeable with different machine brands/models…
    • Torches with amperage adjustment are more complex & not so straightforward when it comes to trying to fit “brand X” torch to “brand Y welder”
    • This is because the control plug is often different from one machine model/brand to another.
    • If existing plug on the old/existing torch is in good condition, this can be re-used and fitted to the replacement torch… however;
    • Torches with remote amperage adjustment have/require multiple wires
    • This means that the wires in the new torch will need to be match to the correct pins on the existing plug. This may require obtaining & consulting plug/control wiring information for the machine
    • Customers are welcome to try to adapt Weldclass torches to other machines, however Weldclass does not guarantee success. For best results we recommend trying to source the original torch from the machine manufacturer first.
  2. Gas Connection
    • Again, different machine brands/models will use different gas connections
    • Refer to description against the specific Weldclass torch for info on gas connection (go to "Details" tab on this page)
    • If 5/8” UNF connection is required, this fitting is available as a separate item - part no P4-RHHCK
  3. Power Cable "Dinse" Connection
    • Most machines 200 Amps & above will have large "35-50" connectors. The Weldclass torches listed on this page are all fitted with "35-50" connectors.

meta.who: Suits home workshops, farm and fencing work, vehicle restoration and light site work where only 10A power or a generator is available.
specs: 2 years standard; 7 years if registered online within 30 days of purchase

faq.q: Can the FORCE 180MST run on a 10A power point?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 180MST is fitted with a 10A 240V plug, so it runs from a standard power point. It still delivers 180A MIG output at 10% duty cycle and has a maximum recommended MIG capacity of 8mm mild steel.

faq.q: Can I run the FORCE 180MST off a generator?
faq.a: Yes. Weldclass rates the FORCE 180MST as generator compatible, with a minimum 8kVA generator and 10kVA recommended. Several owners run it off a generator for fencing and site work, and at 9kg it is easy to carry to the job.

faq.q: Does the FORCE 180MST work with a spool gun?
faq.a: The current FORCE 180MST, released June 2022 with a spool gun switch and socket on the rear, is spool gun ready and suits the optional BZL 25 5m spool gun (WC-06610). The older 180MST model has no spool gun capability, so check the rear panel first.

faq.q: What comes with the FORCE 180MST?
faq.a: The FORCE 180MST standard package (WF-06128, RRP $899 incl. GST) includes the machine, a 3m heavy-duty BZL 25 MIG torch, 3m earth lead, 3m stick lead, gas regulator and hose, and drive rollers for 0.8/0.9mm solid and gasless wire. A TIG torch and trolley are optional extras.

faq.q: What warranty does the FORCE 180MST have?
faq.a: The FORCE 180MST comes with a 2-year standard warranty. Weldclass extends this to 7 years when the machine is registered online within 30 days of purchase, so register it as soon as you buy it from your Weldclass distributor.

meta.who: Suits farm, workshop and light fabrication users who want 15kg spool capacity in a portable machine, with owners using it on shed frames, trailers and long days beside a generator.
specs: 2 years standard; 7 years if registered online within 30 days of purchase

faq.q: What power supply does the FORCE 200MST need?
faq.a: The FORCE 200MST is fitted with a 15A 240V plug, so it needs a 15A outlet or a generator of at least 8kVA (10kVA ideal). In return it delivers 200A MIG output at 25% duty cycle and has a maximum recommended MIG capacity of 10mm mild steel.

faq.q: Does the FORCE 200MST take a 15kg spool?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 200MST takes 15kg (D300mm) spools as well as 5kg (D200mm) spools, which is uncommon for a 13kg machine. Bigger spools mean fewer wire changes on longer jobs. Drive rollers for 0.8/0.9mm solid and gasless wire are included.

faq.q: What comes with the FORCE 200MST?
faq.a: The FORCE 200MST standard package (WF-06129, RRP $1,299 incl. GST) includes the machine, a 4m heavy-duty BZL 25 Euro-fit MIG torch, 4m earth and stick leads, a 2-stage gas regulator and drive rollers for 0.8/0.9mm solid and gasless wire. The spool gun, TIG torch and trolley are optional.

faq.q: What warranty does the FORCE 200MST have?
faq.a: The FORCE 200MST comes with a 2-year standard warranty. Weldclass extends this to 7 years when the machine is registered online within 30 days of purchase, so register it as soon as you buy it from your Weldclass distributor.

Q: Are torch heads available for these torches?

A: Weldclass does not supply the torch head as a separate part. This is because ongoing improvements have been made to both the torch and the torch head design over time (to improve reliability and longevity), and heads are not interchangeable across every different batch/version of the torch. We offer complete torches as listed on this page, which also means that the new/replacement torch will carry any design improvements that the manufacturer has implemented to date.

faq.q: What does PFC do on the FORCE 205MST?
faq.a: Power Factor Correction (PFC) on the FORCE 205MST reduces power draw and increases duty cycle. Weldclass says this makes the 205MST suitable for extension leads up to 100m and for generators of at least 8kVA, ideally 10kVA or more. It helps the machine reach 200A at 30% duty cycle.

faq.q: Is the FORCE 205MST a synergic MIG welder?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 205MST works in manual mode or synergic mode, where you enter the material type and thickness and the machine sets the parameters for you. It has 20+ pre-set programs for different materials and can store custom settings for up to 20 jobs.

faq.q: Does the FORCE 205MST suit aluminium wire?
faq.a: The FORCE 205MST comes with a drive roller for 1.0/1.2mm aluminium wire alongside rollers for 0.8/0.9mm solid and gasless wire, and it is spool gun ready. The optional spool gun is the BZL 25 8m (WC-06203). The wire drive system is geared.

faq.q: Does the FORCE 205MST have VRD?
faq.a: The FORCE 205MST has an optional VRD function for Stick/MMA welding. Machines are supplied with VRD not active. If your site or employer requires VRD, an authorised Weldclass agent or distributor can activate it on the machine.

faq.q: What warranty does the FORCE 205MST have?
faq.a: The FORCE 205MST comes with a 2-year standard warranty. Weldclass extends this to 7 years when the machine is registered online within 30 days of purchase, so register it as soon as you buy it from your Weldclass distributor.

faq.a: The FORCE 255MST needs a generator of at least 13kVA, with 15kVA or more recommended. Its Power Factor Correction (PFC) reduces power draw and increases duty cycle, which Weldclass says also makes the 255MST suitable for extension leads up to 100m.

faq.q: What plug does the FORCE 255MST have?

faq.q: Is the FORCE 255MST a synergic welder?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 255MST can run in manual mode or synergic mode, where you enter the material type and thickness and the machine sets the parameters. It has 20+ pre-set programs and stores custom settings for up to 20 jobs, plus inductance, burnback and 2T/4T trigger adjustments.

faq.q: What warranty does the FORCE 255MST have?
faq.a: The FORCE 255MST comes with a 2-year standard warranty. Weldclass extends this to 7 years when the machine is registered online within 30 days of purchase, so register it as soon as you buy it from your Weldclass distributor.

name: Wire - Hardfacing PLATINUM SD-980 (Solid)
description:
SD-980 hard-facing MIG welding wire is a versatile and easy-to-use "all-rounder". Being a solid wire, PLATINUM SD-980 is easy to apply and is all-positional. Ideal for applications where abrasion resistance is required, and especially when accompanied by shocks and blows. The weld can handle abrasion, moderate-to-high impact and metal-to-metal wear. Commonly used on excavator buckets and teeth, screws and augers, tracks, crushing jaws/wheels, etc. Available in 1.2mm in 15kg or 4.5kg spools. Requires minimum 120 amps. Use with Ar+CO2 mixed gas.
Classification: AS/NZS 2576: 2455-M1

Hardfacing Selection Guide
short: SD-980 hard-facing MIG welding wire is a versatile and easy-to-use "all-rounder". Being a solid wire, PLATINUM SD-980 is easy to apply and is all-positional. Ideal for applications where abrasion resistance is required, and especially when accompanied by shocks and blows. The weld can handle abrasion, moderate-to-high impact and metal-to-metal wear. Commonly used on excavator buckets and teeth, screws and augers, tracks, crushing jaws/wheels, etc. Available in 1.2mm in 15kg or 4.5kg spools. Requires minimum 120 amps. Use with Ar+CO2 mixed gas. Classification: AS/NZS 2576: 2455-M1Hardfacing Selection Guide

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • Versatile "all rounder"
  • Easy to use Solid wire: Use with gas, Use with standard v-groove drive rollers
  • Good abrasion resistance
  • Moderate-to-High impact resistance
  • Especially suited when abrasion is accompanied by shocks and blows
  • All-positional
  • Available in 15kg and 4.5kg spools


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Weld can handle abrasion, moderate-to-high impact and metal-to-metal wear
  • Very suitable for all types of ground engaging equipment; excavator buckets and teeth, points, tynes, screws and augers, tipper bodies
  • Especially suited for components subject to abrasive wear AND impact (shocks & blows); crushing jaws/wheels, etc
  • Also used for metal-to-metal applications such as: excavator tracks, pulleys (incl drag-line pulleys), etc
  • Typical hardness 54-58 HRc / 535-600 HB


OPERATING DATA:

  • Use with Ar-CO2 mixed gas
  • Polarity: DC+ (wire/torch positive, earth negative)
  • Typical parameters: 120-270A @ 19-30V
  • VERY IMPORTANT: Amperage & voltage should be as low as possible within the recommended range. Applying excessive heat/voltage will reduce the performance and wear life of the weld deposit, due to excessive alloying with base material.
  • Buffer layer: Not normally required. In case of hard-to-weld steels, use buffer layer of basic electrodes or flux-cored wire.
  • Pre-Heat: Not normally required, unless to minimise relief-checking (micro cracking)
  • Suitable for multi-layering (up to 3 layers)


FINISH:

  • Surface will normally relief-checks (forms fine cracks) after welding
  • Weld deposit is NOT machineable
  • Weld deposit IS grind-able

CLASSIFICATION:

  • AS/NZS 2576: 2455-M1


SIMILAR & ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS:

  • Hardfacing Wire - Platinum CX-1800 Gasless (very high abrasion & moderate impact)
  • Hardfacing Electrodes - Platinum 943 (very high abrasion & good impact)
  • Hardfacing Electrodes - Promax 700 (general purpose, good abrasion & good impact)


COMPARABLE TO*

  • Stoody 965-G
  • Lincore 55-G/O
  • Robodur K 600-G
  • Welding Alloys L-G/O
  • INE Inefil 600-BR
  • Postalloy 2898-SPL / PHF 650G
  • Talweld EA600, Talarc HF600
  • Hobart Tubealloy 258-0
  • Hobart Vertiwear 600

*Comparable products are given for indicative purposes only, the characteristics and properties of each different brand & type of product will not be identical. Any reference to brand names or trade names of comparable products are the property of their respective owners and have no affiliation with Weldclass.

name: PROMAX GP Electrodes (General Purpose)
description:
The Weldclass Promax GP is an easy-to-use, all-positional welding rod for mild & galvanised steels, supplied in a 1kg re-usable convenience pack to keep electrodes in good condition. Very smooth arc, easy re-striking & easy slag removal. Fast-freezing slag formula, for welding in all positions including vertial down. Tolerant to dirty materials and poor fit-up. Available in 2.0mm, 2.6mm & 3.2mm.
If a more forceful arc is desired, and for larger volume applications, we recommend the best-selling Weldclass Platinum 12V electrode .

name: Electrodes - Hardfacing PLATINUM 943
description:
High-performance hard-facing welding rod, ideal for ground-engaging equipment. Platinum 943 deposits extremely hard, abrasion resistant CrNb carbides, offering long wear life with both exceptional abrasion resistance and impact strength. Ideal for hard surfacing applications where resistance to high or extreme abrasion (in particular sliding abrasion) and moderate to heavy impact are required.
Due to the nodular shape of the complex carbides, Platinum 943 deposits are capable of withstanding heavier impact levels than standard chromium-carbide electrodes. Typical applications include; buckets, lips, screws, hammers, teeth, crushing equipment, etc. Typical hardness 60-65 HRC (1st layer). Supplied in a 1kg re-usable convenience pack to keep electrodes in good condition.

Stick Electrode Selection Chart Hardfacing Selection Guide

  • Capable of withstanding heavier impact levels than standard chromium-carbide electrodes


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Extremely hard, abrasion-resistant Chromium 22% + Niobium (CrNb) 7% deposit
  • Ideal for hard surfacing applications where resistance to high or extreme abrasion (in particular sliding abrasion) and moderate to heavy impact are required.
  • Typical applications include; buckets, lips, screws, hammers, teeth, crushing equipment, etc.
  • NOT recommended for: metal-to-metal wear


OPERATING INFO:

  • Polarity: DC+ or AC+ (electrode +)
  • Typical current range: 3.2mm 115-140A / 4.0mm 140-185A
  • Positions: Horizonal / Flat
  • Recommended stick out 15-20mm
  • To prevent dilution of hardness, avoid high current
  • Max 3 layers
  • Minimum recommended OCV ( open circuit voltage ): 55V*

*Most inverter welding machines have OCV of 55V or more. Some older transformer machines may have OCV of less than 55V and may not be ideal for running these electrodes. OCV rating will normally be shown on machine data plate, indicated by the symbol "Uo" .


TYPICAL PROPERTIES OF ALL WELD METAL:

  • Hardness: Single layer 60-65HRC, Multi-layer 64-69HRC
  • Composition %: C0.50 Mn0.70 Cr22.0 Nb7.0 FeBal'


FINISHING:

  • Relief cracking is normal (surface will form fine cracks after welding)
  • Weld deposit is NOT machineable
  • Weld deposit IS grind-able

name: Wire - Hardfacing PLATINUM CX-1800 (Gasless)
description:
Long-Life hardfacing 'MIG' wire for ground-engaging equipment. Very high resistance to abrasion with up to 3-4 times better wear life vs other common hardfacing wires* thanks to high Cr content (~26%) and special additives.
Recommended for metal-to-earth applications where wear is mostly caused by abrasion, with low-to-medium impact; points, tynes, buckets, teeth, screws, augers, grousers, etc.
Gasless wire for easy application. Available in 1.2mm in 15kg or 4.5kg spools. Requires minimum 140 amps, suitable for use with 200A-250A MIG welders.
Classification: AS/NZS 2576: 2360-B7

Hardfacing Selection Guide
short: Long-Life hardfacing 'MIG' wire for ground-engaging equipment. Very high resistance to abrasion with up to 3-4 times better wear life vs other common hardfacing wires thanks to high Cr content (~26%) and special additives. Recommended for metal-to-earth applications where wear is mostly caused by abrasion, with low-to-medium impact; points, tynes, buckets, teeth, screws, augers, grousers, etc. Gasless wire for easy application. Available in 1.2mm in 15kg or 4.5kg spools. Requires minimum 140 amps, suitable for use with 200A-250A MIG welders. Classification: AS/NZS 2576: 2360-B7 Hardfacing Selection Guide

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • High-performance, 3-4 times longer wear life vs other common wires*
  • Very high abrasion resistance
  • Light-to-medium impact resistance
  • Gasless flux-cored wire, easy application in the field or workshop
  • Available in 15kg and 4.5kg spools


APPLICATION INFO:

  • Typical hardness 59-61 HRc / 615-645 HB (max hardness achieved with 2 layers)
  • Ideal for ground-engaging agricultural and earthmoving tools subject to high abrasion and low-to-moderate impact


SURFACE PREPARATION:

  • VERY IMPORTANT: Surface to be hard faced must be clean and free of rust, scale, grease, moisture & other contamination.
  • If existing/old hardfacing deposits are loose they should be removed. (Hammer test can confirm bond strength of existing deposits, a "ping" indicates good bond and a "clack" indicates a separation layer which must be ground off).
  • Buffer Layer / Pre-Heat: CX-1800 will typically weld easily to most common surfaces WITHOUT the need for buffer layer or pre-heat, such as mild & high carbon steel, cast steel, etc.
  • If applying to hard-to-weld steels, or hard-to-weld existing deposits, use buffer layer of 309 or 312 wire or electrodes. Whilst not essential, pre-heat of 150-350c may be beneficial.
  • If applying to high-manganese (non-magnetic) steel, buffer of specialist high-Mn/Cr wire should be used.


OPERATING DATA:

  • Polarity: DC+ (torch/wire positive)
  • Typical parameters: 140-200A @ 18-22V
  • VERY IMPORTANT: Amperage & voltage should be as low as possible within the recommended range. Applying excessive heat/voltage will reduce the performance and wear life of the weld deposit, due to excessive alloying with base material.
  • Layers: Suitable for multi-layering (up to 3 layers)
  • Positions: Flat / downhand only (not suitable for vertical or overhead)


FINISH:

  • Surface normally relief-checks (forms fine micro cracks) after welding
  • Weld deposit is NOT machineable
  • Weld deposit IS grind-able


CLASSIFICATION:

  • AS/NZS 2576: 2360-B7


SIMILAR & ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS:

  • Hardfacing Electrodes - Promax 700 (general purpose, moderate abrasion & good impact)
  • Hardfacing Electrodes - Platinum 943 (very high abrasion & good impact)
  • Hardfacing Wire - Platinum SD-980 Solid (moderate abrasion & good impact, all-positional)


*3-4 times longer wear life vs other common hardfacing wires with Cr content <10%. Actual performance will vary depending on application and use conditions, trials should be conducted to determine how a specific wire will perform in any given application situation.

SUPERIOR TO "ROLL" TYPE FILTERS:

name: Wire - Hardfacing PLATINUM CX-2150 (Gasless)
description:
Extreme performance hardfacing 'MIG' wire, providing a unique combination of both extreme abrasion resistance AND high impact resistance. Up to 6-7 times better wear life vs basic hardfacing wires*... thanks to special carbide additives not found in other wires.
Suitable for a very wide range of applications such as; components subject to abrasion together with high impact stress, where down-time cost is high and longer service life is critical for reducing costs, and where the exact nature of wear is not known in advance and all-round abrasion + impact protection is needed.
Typical applications include: metal-to-earth, ground-engaging equipment, crushing, dredging, mining equipment, grizzly bars, and much more.
Gasless wire for easy application. Available in 1.6mm. Requires minimum 160 amps, suitable for use with MIG welders around 200A-250A & above.

Hardfacing Selection Guide
short: Extreme performance hardfacing 'MIG' wire, providing a unique combination of both extreme abrasion resistance AND high impact resistance. Up to 6-7 times better wear life vs basic hardfacing wires... thanks to special carbide additives not found in other wires.Suitable for a very wide range of applications such as; components subject to abrasion together with high impact stress, where down-time cost is high and longer service life is critical for reducing costs, and where the exact nature of wear is not known in advance and all-round abrasion + impact protection is needed.

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES:

  • Extreme performance, offering extreme abrasion resistance AND high impact resistance
  • Wear life of up to 6-7 times basic hardfacing wires
  • Gasless flux-cored wire, easy to use with very low slag levels
  • Typical hardness 61-63 HRc / 645-680 HB (max hardness achieved with 2 layers)


TYPICAL APPLICATIONS:

  • Components subject to abrasion together with high impact stress
  • Where down-time cost is high and longer service life is critical for reducing costs
  • Where the exact nature of wear is not known in advance, and all-round abrasion + impact protection is needed
  • Metal-to-earth, ground-engaging equipment, crushing, dredging, mining equipment, grizzly bars, and much more


SURFACE PREPARATION:

  • VERY IMPORTANT: Surface to be hard faced must be clean and free of rust, scale, grease, moisture & other contamination.
  • If existing/old hardfacing deposits are loose they should be removed. (Hammer test can confirm bond strength of existing deposits, a "ping" indicates good bond and a "clack" indicates a separation layer which must be ground off).
  • Buffer Layer / Pre-Heat: CX-2150 will typically weld easily to most common surfaces WITHOUT the need for buffer layer or pre-heat, such as mild & high carbon steel, cast steel, etc.
  • If applying to hard-to-weld steels, or hard-to-weld existing deposits, use buffer layer of 309 or 312 wire or electrodes. Whilst not essential, pre-heat of 150-350c may be beneficial.
  • If applying to high-manganese (non-magnetic) steel, buffer of specialist high-Mn/Cr wire should be used.


OPERATING DATA:

  • Polarity: DC+ (torch/wire positive)
  • Typical parameters: 160-240A @ 20-26V
  • VERY IMPORTANT: Amperage & voltage should be as low as possible within the recommended range. Applying excessive heat/voltage will reduce the performance and wear life of the weld deposit, due to excessive alloying with base material.
  • Layers: Suitable for multi-layering (up to 3 layers), optimal performance/hardness is achieved in the 2nd layer
  • Positions: Flat / downhand only (not suitable for vertical or overhead)


FINISH:

  • Surface normally relief-checks (forms fine micro cracks) after welding
  • Weld deposit is NOT machineable
  • Weld deposit IS grind-able


SIMILAR & ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS:

  • Hardfacing Electrodes - Platinum 943 (very high abrasion & good impact)
  • Hardfacing Wire - Platinum CX-1800 Gasless (high abrasion & low-medium impact)
  • Hardfacing Wire - Platinum SD-980 Solid (moderate abrasion & good impact, all-positional)

meta.summary: The PROMAX 180 is an entry-level auto-darkening welding helmet for occasional MIG and Stick welding. It has variable shade 9-13, sensitivity and delay adjustment, 1/1/1/2 optics and a 96 x 39mm viewing area. RRP $89.
meta.who: Suits beginners, hobbyists and home workshop users who weld occasionally with MIG or Stick.
specs: Full laminate, Hinge and Lock retainer
2 years standard on the auto-darkening lens, 7-year offer with online registration within 30 days of purchase

faq.q: Who is the PROMAX 180 welding helmet for?
faq.a: The PROMAX 180 Welding Helmet is designed for occasional MIG and Stick welding. It suits beginners and home users who want an auto-darkening helmet at an RRP of $89. Weldclass says it is built to the same standard as its higher-end PROMAX models.

faq.q: Does the PROMAX 180 have a grind mode?
faq.a: No grind mode is listed for the PROMAX 180 Welding Helmet. Its functions are variable shade 9-13 plus sensitivity and delay adjustments. If you want a grind-mode switch, the PROMAX 200 adds one and is otherwise similar, with an RRP of $110.

faq.q: What is the viewing area of the PROMAX 180?
faq.a: The PROMAX 180 Welding Helmet has a 96 x 39mm viewing area with 1/1/1/2 rated optics. The lens uses full laminate construction, and the Hinge and Lock retainer makes cover lens replacement easy. A magnification lens holder takes standard magnification lenses.

faq.q: What warranty comes with the PROMAX 180?
faq.a: The PROMAX 180 Welding Helmet has a 2-year standard warranty on the auto-darkening lens. Weldclass offers an extended 7-year warranty on the lens, which requires online registration within 30 days of purchase. It is sold through Weldclass distributors at an RRP of $89 incl. GST.

  • Extra-large 80cm 2 viewing area
  • 'Landscape' 108mm wide x 74mm high window/screen format for wider & more natural field of view
  • Ultra-Crisp optics with enhanced color recognition

APPLICATION INFO:

  • MIG welding
  • Stick welding
  • TIG welding down to 5 amps
  • Grinding
  • Plasma Cutting
  • Oxy Cutting, Brazing, Heating
  • Gouging


FUNCTIONS:

  • Welding mode: Variable shade 9-14
  • Cut mode: Variable shade 4-8
  • Grind mode: Locks lens to light mode (shade 3)
  • Shade Lock: Switches off auto-darkening function & locks lens to a selected shade level (4-13), ideal for oxy cutting & similar processes where conditions may not be ideal for normal auto-darkening function
  • Memory: Save up to 10 favorite settings (recalls shade, sensitivity & delay settings)

  • Gradient Mode: Gradual return (slope down) from dark to light, mirrors cooling of the weld pool to reduce eye strain
  • Sensitivity: Adjustable 0-9 settings


OTHER FEATURES:

  • High-Impact tested and rated to Australian standard AS1337.1
  • Auto-darkening lens complies with AS1338.1
  • Easy cover lens replacement

  • Full-Laminate Lens Construction: Each layer in the electronic lens assembly is firmly laminated for superior optical quality and long service life. This is in contrast to cheaper lenses which are simply glued on the edge and, over time, are prone to contamination and failure.

  • Auto-on & Auto-off = No buttons to press, Hassle-Free operation

faq.q: What does the external grind button on the PROMAX 650 do?
faq.a: The PROMAX 650 Welding Helmet has a grind button on the outside of the shell. Pressing it locks the lens at shade 3 so you can switch between welding and grinding without removing or lifting the helmet. Grind mode can also be set through the internal controls.

faq.q: Can the PROMAX 650 be used for oxy cutting?
faq.a: Yes. The PROMAX 650 Welding Helmet has a shade lock function that turns off auto-darkening and holds the lens at a chosen shade from 4 to 13. Weldclass recommends this for oxy cutting and similar processes where normal auto-darkening may not switch reliably.

faq.q: How many settings can the PROMAX 650 save?
faq.a: The PROMAX 650 Welding Helmet can store up to 10 favourite settings in memory. Each one recalls shade, sensitivity and delay, which makes it quick to move between processes such as MIG and TIG. It also has a gradient mode that eases the lens back from dark to light.

faq.q: How heavy is the PROMAX 650?
faq.a: The PROMAX 650 Welding Helmet weighs 580g. Weldclass says it is up to 15% lighter than other digital wide-view helmets. It uses wrap-around headgear with a moulded rear pressure pad, and has an RRP of $299 incl. GST in matte black through Weldclass distributors.

faq.q: What warranty does the PROMAX 650 have?
faq.a: The PROMAX 650 Welding Helmet has a 2-year standard warranty on the auto-darkening lens. Weldclass offers an extended 7-year warranty on the lens, which requires online registration within 30 days of purchase. The helmet complies with AS1337.1 and the lens with AS1338.1.

description:
PLATINUM TK Super-Flex series torches offer exceptional flexibility and control, even in the most delicate and demanding TIG applications. Designed for use on professional TIG welding machines (such as AC/DC), where a light weight, flexible and slimline / low-profile torch is preferred.
Can be used together with a foot controller/pedal, or as a switched torch using the optional trigger kit.

meta.more:
KEY FEATURES

  • Available with leading 7-Year Warranty*
  • Super-flex 1-piece cable, flexi torch head & slimline handle
  • Universal fit: Includes range of different gas fittings to suit different machines
  • Ready-to-weld, with parts kit included

INCLUDES

  • Super-Flex braided 1-piece cable (power & gas in one cable)
  • Cylindrical low-profile torch handle to allow pencil-grip
  • Flexible torch #17F head (without valve)
  • "Ready-to-weld" parts kits with 1pc each: 57Y02 Long Back Cap, 10N23 1.6mm Collet, 10N31 1.6mm Collet Body, 10N47 Ceramic Cup, 1.6mm Rare Earth Tungsten Electrode
  • Large '35-50' (Ø13mm) male connector to suit most welders 180-200A & above
  • Gas fittings: Ø9mm quick-connect male plug (fitted) + additional threaded gas fittings to suit most brands/models of TIG welding machines (5/8UNF male, M12x1 female, 3/8BSP female)*
  • Water hose fittings (TK18 torch only): Ø9mm quick-connect male plugs

*For fitting torch to machines that have threaded gas outlet, cut off the existing quick-connect fitting and replace with the applicable threaded fitting, using hose nipple/barb and hose clamps supplied with torch

TYPICAL APPLICATION

For use on professional TIG welding machines (typically AC/DC machines), where a light weight, flexible and slimline torch is preferred for maximum dexterity & control, and:

  • Operator is using a foot pedal / foot controller. Valve, switch & other controls on the torch head are NOT required, as all controls/adjustments are made via the foot pedal.
  • OR, optional trigger kit is fitted to allow on/off control on the torch, with all other controls via either machine control panel, or with a foot pedal.

OTHER SPECIFICATIONS

  • TK17 series: 150 amp max capacity: suitable for use with tungsten electrodes up to 2.4mm, and for welding materials up to approx' 3mm thickness
  • TK18 water-cooled series: 350 amp max capacity
  • Suits all Weldclass AC/DC TIG machines & most other brands and models of professional and AC/DC TIG welders
  • Not recommended for use with 'basic' TIG welders that do not have integrated/internal TIG gas line (f or this application, use Weldclass 17FV/26FV series torches, which have valved head and extended gas hose with 5/8" female fitting for direct connection to gas bottle/regulator)

*Standard warranty 3 months, with extended 7 year warranty available if registered online after purchase.

  • Plasma Cutting
  • Oxy Cutting, Brazing, Heating

  • Shade adjustment: Auto (shade level adjusts automatically depending on arc intensity) or Manual (user adjusts), adjust in increments of +/- 0.5 via external or internal controls

  • Welding mode: Variable shade 9-14
  • Cut mode: Variable shade 4-8
  • Grind mode: Locks lens to light mode (shade 3), activate on/off via external button or internal controls

  • Delay (switching time from dark back to light after welding stops): Auto or Manual 0.1-1.0s
  • Gradient Mode: Gradual return (slope down) from dark to light, mirrors cooling of the weld pool to reduce eye strain
  • Sensitivity: Auto or Manual 0-9 settings
  • Tack Mode: Returns to shade 5 (inead of shade 3) between welds to reduce fatigue

faq.q: What is in the FORCE 132MST Ready Kit?
faq.a: The FORCE 132MST Ready Kit (WC-132MSTRK, RRP $369 incl. GST) includes the machine with a 2m BZL 15 torch, 2m earth lead, 2m stick lead, a 0.45kg roll of 0.9mm gasless wire, knurled gasless drive roller, welding gloves, wire brush with chipping hammer and spare MIG tips.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 132MST weld with gas?
faq.a: Yes, with extra parts. To MIG weld with solid wire and shielding gas, the FORCE 132MST needs the optional gas regulator (4-AR1), gas hose kit (WC-03338) and a v-groove drive roller. The machine already has a quick-connect gas inlet and an electric gas solenoid valve built in.

faq.q: Can the FORCE 132MST weld aluminium?
faq.a: No. Weldclass does not recommend the FORCE 132MST for MIG welding aluminium, and it cannot TIG weld aluminium because that needs AC/DC TIG capability, such as the FORCE 201T. It suits solid mild steel, stainless and gasless flux-cored wire, plus DC lift-arc TIG of steel, stainless, copper and chromoly up to 2-3mm.

faq.q: Is the FORCE 132MST suitable for trade use?
faq.a: Weldclass positions the FORCE 132MST for serious hobbyist and occasional light trade or maintenance use. For regular trade, field or site work it recommends the FORCE 160MST or above, which have heavier-duty Euro-connect torches and wire drive systems.

faq.q: What warranty does the FORCE 132MST have?
faq.a: The FORCE 132MST comes with a 1-year standard warranty. Weldclass extends this to 7 years when the machine is registered online within 30 days of purchase, so register it as soon as you buy it from your Weldclass distributor.

KEY FEATURES

  • High-tech proprietary coating provides superior performance & safety vs most other types of high-temperature blankets
  • Max recommended working temperature / exposure: 1200°c
  • Max short term / momentary heat resistance: ~1600°c
  • Coating on both sides of blanket completely seals / impregnates base fibres, providing a smooth, non-hairy finish
  • Non-irritant, very safe, comfortable and easy to handle
  • Resists spark penetration between fibres that can occur with other blankets
  • Does NOT shed dust / fibres, which is an eye / skin / respiratory hazard associated with most other high-temp blankets
  • Does not give off toxic / harmful fumes when in contact with heat / flame
  • Smooth surface enables spatter and dross to cascade away, when used as a drape with blanket on an inclined surface
  • Strong, durable, tear-resistant, and abrasion-resistant
  • Lightweight: special coating allows WB1250+ fabric to be lightweight, whilst offering protection that would usually only be achieved with much thicker & heavier fabrics
  • Safer & easier handling and transport (1x23m roll weighs ~12kg), compared to other blanket rolls that can weight up to 50kg or more
  • Resistant oils and solvents (which can contaminate blankets and become a fire hazard)
  • Can be easily cut to any required length or shape using knife or scissors, leaving a smooth edge that resists fraying, and with no shedding of raw fibres that cause irritation

APPLICATION INFO*

  • For protection against sparks, spatter, light molten metal splash, and intermittent flame
  • Suitable for protecting objects during grinding, welding, oxy cutting, gouging, etc
  • Not recommended for heat treatment / stress relieving (wrapping of heated objects to slow cooling). For this application, fabrics/blankets with a higher density / weight (such as Promax WB550 , WB1000 , or WB1100 ) are recommended for maximum heat insulation / retention.
  • Withstands intermittent short-duration flame exposure, however not recommended for prolonged / constant direct flame exposure. For resistance against longer-duration flame exposure, Promax WB1100 is more suitable.

SPECIFICATIONS

  • Max recommended working temperature / exposure: 1200°c
  • Max short term / momentary heat resistance: ~1600°c
  • Nominal Thickness: 0.5mm
  • Nominal Weight: 500g/m2
  • Colour: Grey
  • Base fabric: Glass fibre with special proprietary non-toxic, inorganic, non-flammable coating

INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE

  • If protecting critical or costly surfaces / items, allways use more layers initially, and test on a non-critical surface first
  • When using for surface protection: If possible use on an incline of at least 15 degrees, or when neccessary to use in horizontal position add more layers
  • Where the blanket is in closer proximity to the source of sparks etc, consider adding more layers of blanket/fabric as the sparks/spatter will have less time to cool and will be at a higher temperature at the point of touching/impact with the blanket
  • Cut blanket to any required length or shape using sharp knife or scissors
  • Does not require any special PPE to handle the blanket itself, however use of eye, hand, and respiratory protection is always recommend for protection against any dust & debris that has fallen on the blanket during use

*As applications and usage conditions vary widely, no warranty or fitness for use in any specific application is implied or intended. In critical applications, blankets should always be tested/trialed to determined if they offer adequate protection. E.&O.E.

  • Withstands intermittent short-duration flame exposure, however not recommended for prolonged / constant direct flame exposure. For resistance against longer-duration flame exposure, Promax WB1100 is more suitable.

SPECIFICATIONS

  • Max recommended working temperature / exposure: 800 ° c
  • Max short term / momentary heat resistance: ~1000°c
  • Nominal Thickness: 1.5mm (~3mm at hem)
  • Nominal Weight: 1,100g/m2
  • Colour: Golden brown
  • Base fabric: Glass fibre

INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE

  • If protecting critical or costly surfaces / items, allways use more layers initially, and test on a non-critical surface first
  • When using for surface protection: If possible use on an incline of at least 15 degrees, or when neccessary to use in horizontal position add more layers
  • Where the blanket is in closer proximity to the source of sparks etc, consider adding more layers of blanket/fabric as the sparks/spatter will have less time to cool and will be at a higher temperature at the point of touching/impact with the blanket
  • Use hand, eye and respiratory protection during handling and use, to protect against airborn fibres and any dust/debris that has fallen on the blanket during use
  • While blanket will withstand up to 800-1,000 ° c , a safety margin should always be allowed for, especially in critical applications. Recommended maximum long-duration direct contact temperature exposure is 600-700 ° c.
  • Consider using WB1100 or WB1250+ blankets for more demanding applications
  • Worn or damaged blankets will compromise protection and should be replaced

*As applications and usage conditions vary widely, no warranty or fitness for use in any specific application is implied or intended. In critical applications, blankets should always be tested/trialed to determined if they offer adequate protection. E.&O.E.

faq.q: What filter does the PROMAX R50 respirator use?
faq.a: The PROMAX R50 respirator supplied with the PROMAX 850R Welding Helmet uses a 3-stage system: a TH3 (P3) main particle filter, a carbon prefilter for nuisance odours and a spark filter. TH3 class delivers 99.8% or better particle purity and is designed for welding fume particulate.

faq.q: How long does the PROMAX 850R battery last?
faq.a: The Li-ion battery in the PROMAX 850R Welding Helmet's R50 respirator runs for 10 hours or more at 170 L/min, or 6 hours or more at the top 230 L/min setting. A bonus second battery is included, so one can charge while the other is in use.

faq.q: Can you grind with the PROMAX 850R?
faq.a: Yes. The PROMAX 850R Welding Helmet has a flip-up welding lens with a large clear grinding visor behind it, so you can grind under filtered air without removing the helmet. Shade 5 side windows give peripheral vision while welding.

faq.q: How heavy is the PROMAX 850R with respirator?
faq.a: The PROMAX 850R Welding Helmet weighs 940g on its own, and the R50 respirator with blower unit and hose weighs 930g, for a combined 1.87kg. The blower is carried on a 4-point waist and shoulder harness, and the shoulder straps can be removed.

faq.q: What warranty applies to the PROMAX 850R?
faq.a: The PROMAX 850R Welding Helmet carries a 7-year warranty offer on the electronic lens, which requires online registration within 30 days of purchase. The R50 blower unit has a 2-year warranty and the battery 1 year. RRP is $1,148 incl. GST through Weldclass distributors.

  • Remote amp +/- controls on MIG torch handpiece
  • Push-Pull Ready: Software pre-configured & ready for use with optional Push-Pull MIG Torch
  • Job Save to capture specific parameters / settings with custom naming and easy recall for the next time you need to repeat the same job/weld
  • USB interface allows fast & easy software upgrades throughout the life of the machine, plus importing & exporting of saved settings between multiple 220MP machines

  • Compact and portable, weighs 22kg
  • Takes D200mm (5kg steel / 2kg Alu) or D300mm (15kg steel / 6-7kg Alu) spools
  • Large "35-50" cable connections

APPLICATION & CAPABILITY INFO*

  • Single or Double Pulse MIG welding 20-220A with Aluminium (0.8-1.2mm wires / 0.8-5.0/6.0mm material*), Stainless-Steel (0.8-1.0mm wires / 0.8-5.0mm material), & Bronze/Brazing (0.8-0.9mm wires / 0.8-5.0mm material)
  • Conventional Non-Pulse MIG welding 20-220A with solid mild steel (0.6-1.2mm wires / 0.5-10mm material), stainless-steel (0.8-1.0mm wires), aluminium (0.8-1.2mm wires / 3-8mm material) & bronze/brazing (0.8-0.9mm wires)
  • Pulse MIG welding with optional Push-Pull MIG Torch and 0.8-1.2mm wires
  • Stick/MMA welding 20-160A with most types of common electrodes (2.0-4.0mm), including steel, stainless-steel, hardfacing & more

FUNCTIONS

  • PoP (Pulse-on-Pulse / Double Pulse) mode
  • AB Pulse (Single Pulse) mode

  • Pulse wave adjustments: Start Current amps/time, Start-Slope time, Main Current, Secondary Current & Frequency (double pulse), End Slope time, End Current amps/time
  • Root MIG mode: Used with mild steel wire only. Enables gap-filling & first-pass (root) welding of pieces that are spaced apart (poor fit-up, gaps, cracks, etc) that traditionally would only be achievable by TIG welding. Weld pool is typically colder than the arc for very low heat & minimal distortion.
  • Trigger modes: 2T, 4T & unique 4T Bi-Level which allows the operator to "manually double-pulse" (manually switch between primary and secondary current levels by quickly pulling then releasing the trigger)
  • Other MIG Adjustments include: Arc Length, Inductance, Soft Start, Burnback, Pre-Gas time, Post-Gas time, Spot Weld time
  • Stick/MMA Adjustments include: Hot-Start %, Arc-Force %

⚠️ Safety Guidelines For Handling of Thoriated Tungsten Electrodes ⚠️

Important Notice:
Thoriated Tungsten electrodes contain low-level radioactive thorium. Improper handling may pose health and environmental risks. Follow these safety guidelines and comply with all applicable local regulations.

Regulatory Compliance:
Check with local authorities: Disposal and handling requirements vary by region. Consult your local environmental, radiation safety, or hazardous waste management authority for specific guidance.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):
Always wear gloves and a mask when handling Thoriated Tungsten or its dust.
Use a respirator if grinding or sanding to prevent inhalation of radioactive particles.
Avoid skin contact and ingestion.

Waste Handling and Storage:
Collect all dust and waste in a sealed, clearly labelled container.
Store the container in a designated, secure area until it can be transported to an approved disposal facility.
Do not dispose of Thoriated Tungsten waste in general rubbish or wastewater systems.

Liability Disclaimer:
Failure to follow these safety procedures may result in personal injury, environmental harm, or legal consequences. Weldclass takes no responsibility for misuse, or non-compliance with your local regulations.

faq.q: What welding can the ALLCLEAR MT84 be used with?
faq.a: The ALLCLEAR MT84 On-Torch Fume Extractor is for gas MIG, gasless and flux-cored welding. It must not be used where fume contains aluminium dust, oil mist, gases or water vapour. Aluminium dust can be explosive when airborne, and water vapour damages the filter.

faq.q: How does auto on/off work on the ALLCLEAR MT84?
faq.a: The ALLCLEAR MT84 On-Torch Fume Extractor can start and stop automatically with the MIG torch trigger. Pass the welder's earth lead through the current-sensing clip on top of the unit. Manual on/off is also available, and each of the two motors can be switched separately.

faq.q: Which torch works with the ALLCLEAR MT84?
faq.a: The ALLCLEAR MT84 On-Torch Fume Extractor is designed to plug into the ALLCLEAR FT36E 4m fume-extraction MIG torch, which is rated 320A and uses BZL 36 consumables. The supplied 3m hose has no torch-end fitting, so check fittings with your torch supplier for other brands.

faq.q: What filter does the ALLCLEAR MT84 use?
faq.a: The ALLCLEAR MT84 On-Torch Fume Extractor uses a HEPA H13 filter rated 99.95% at 0.3 micron, with 4m² of PTFE-coated conical anti-clog media. HEPA is standard on units Weldclass supplies from September 2026. Earlier units used an M-class PTFE 99.9% filter.

faq.q: Can the ALLCLEAR MT84 run two torches?
faq.a: Yes, with the Dual Torch Upgrade Kit (W06818, RRP $1,499). It adds a second FT36E 4m torch, a 3m x 44mm hose, an adaptor and an inlet assembly to the ALLCLEAR MT84 On-Torch Fume Extractor. The kit only fits MT84 units manufactured in or after 2026.

Flame-retardant (FR) caps made from treated cotton are intended to provide limited protection from sparks and light spatter during general welding and cutting work. The fabric is chemically treated to resist ignition, however it is not flameproof and will not protect against molten metal or heavy spatter or direct contact with flame. FR cotton caps are not suitable for heavy fabrication, gouging, or overhead welding where exposure to intense sparks, molten metal, or dross may occur. In higher-risk applications, more substantial protective equipment such as leather welding apparel and appropriate head protection should be used. Users must assess their specific working conditions and select suitable protective equipment accordingly. Proper welding PPE, including helmets, clothing, gloves, and other protective gear, should always be used.

reviews.c: Brilliant machine! Very happy with warranty though with the quality of the machine I don't expect there to be too many problems. 10/10!

The last time I bought a mig welder was in 1995 a 185 Esab unit that worked very well & now is in possession of good friend & still going strong. I decided it was time for a new mig & through much seaching reading & deciding on how much I wanted to spend the 205MPST Fury ticked the boxes I needed ticking. I hold various welding certifications & consider myself a very competent welder. I was a little hesistant about using the Synergic mode but decided to try it on the first lot of welds on the project I needed to weld up. Out of the box, set up & with a base tune from the recommended settings from inside the wire feeder door I was able to put down a great looking & very sound weld. Using the trim function I was able to fine tune the machine to suit a variety of different weld types that suited my style of welding. I wish I could show the welds they all look so good, with great fusion, re-enforcement, no cold lap or undercut on the welds. With various mig welders I have used over the years what pleasantly surprised me the most was the start came in hot, no lumpy cold weld, burnt into the beginning of a previous weld again with perfect fusion & near absolute zero splatter. I am very happy with my purchase, I have yet to explore the many other features this welder offers, but feel it will perform as expected. Would I recommend this to friends, colleagues, highly yes. Also I feel this would be a great welder for a pro through to a novice. I feel someone with minimal training could put down sound welds with this welding unit. As with any structural welds then only a trained person should be doing those welds. For the home project builder this welder would be a great addition to the shed.
